To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytokine, tumournecrosis factor alpha (Tnfα), activates a protection signalling cascade during ischamic postconditioning (IpostC).
TNF-alpha plays a bidirectional role associated with the severity comorbidities, and that diabetic and/or mildly obese patients may still derive benefit from ischaemic post-conditioning.
TNF knockout mice are more susceptible to ischaemia-reperfusion injury and are not protected from ischaemic post-conditioning, but that this is not observed in obese or diabetic wild-type mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of obesity and diabetes on the outcome of ischaemic post-conditioning.
the role of tumour necrosis alpha in the outcome of ischaemic post-conditioning and the impact of obesity and diabetes.
a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of obesity and diabetes and the role of TNFα in IPostC in the presence of obesity and diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TNFα plays a protective role in IPostC in the absence of obesity and diabetes.
TNFα is a key player in the protection afforded by IPostC in control animals but not in obese and diabetic animals.
the outcome of IpostC is influenced by TNFα in a complex manner, which may be dependent on the severity of comorbidities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity and diabetes alter the cytokine profile in a way that TNFα may be beneficial in the presence of modest obesity and detrimental in the presence of diabetes.
obesity and diabetes alter the cytokine profile and the outcome of IpostC in the mouse model.
TNFα plays a protective role during IPostC in control mice, but not in mice with concomitant obesity and diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IPostC is still beneficial in obese or diabetic animals, but that the protective effect of this strategy is reduced in these conditions.
TNFα may be an important therapeutic target in obese and diabetic patients undergoing IPostC.
the outcome of ischaemic post-conditioning in obese and/or diabetic mice depends on the severity of comorbidities.
